name: jp3d
description: Jurassic Park 3D (Ocean, PC386 v1.31, 11/04/93) under DOSBox-X -- the first-person half of the game, JP3D.EXE. The data segment is JP3D.EXE's load segment plus 0xB99, which its own entry sets with `mov ax,<load>+0xb99; mov ds,ax`; the load segment is not fixed, so the segment is found by pattern rather than assumed. It is recognised by 100 bytes of the asset path literals at DS:0x0D39 -- shipped data, byte-identical between the recovered image and a running guest, and unique in conventional memory. NOTE the game cannot usefully be started on its own: like JP2D it wants the launcher's GAMEEMS handle and the 93-byte shared block, and without them PROGRAM keeps whatever the image ships and the section, language and sound devices are not the ones the chain would have chosen. Launch dosbox-x/jp3d_chain.conf after `python tools/chain_stub.py --step 0 --cursor 0x18 --write`, which stands in for the mouse-driven front end and resumes the launcher at its JP3D entry. Driving is by AUTOTYPE in the .conf: like JP2D, the game installs its own INT 9 handler and never reads the BIOS keyboard ring.

marker.note: The tail of the blockset name template, the two palette paths and the debug-overlay labels that follow them, 100 bytes from DS:0x0D39.  Static, and it occurs exactly once in conventional memory.  The level table's own map paths at DS:0x0050 look equally good and are not: their descriptors sit beside words the loader rewrites.

checks.note: 'RESOURCE.3D\0', the container name the 3D game's opener passes to INT 21h AH=3D
'Dark.pal\0Day.pal\0', the two 57,344-byte shade tables 1000:5506 chooses between
the near plane, a constant no instruction writes; see docs/RENDER3D.md

'mapsis1.map�', the first of the eleven map paths the sixteen-slot level table at DS:0x002C names. Read the geometry_segment symbol to tell whether the arena has actually run: it is zero until 1000:7160 has.

mouse.note: JP3D does not use the mouse; only the OPTIONS front end does. dosbox_click is not useful for the game.

screen.note: Mode 13h, but the 3D view is only the middle 224x130 of it -- DS:0x8188 selects the viewport and ships zero, so the wide 304x184 arm is unreachable. The rest of the screen is lbm\panel.bit. The renderer draws into the 65,536-byte arena buffer at DS:0xBEB8 and blits from there, so a mid-frame capture shows a whole frame rather than a partial one.

asset_paths.description: The asset path table; the profile marker.

resource_name.description: 'RESOURCE.3D', passed to INT 21h AH=3D by the opener.

program.description: The shared block's PROGRAM field, copied here only when the launcher supplied one. `and bx,7` picks one of the five sections.

level.description: The current level index, an index into the sixteen-slot table at DS:0x002C. Eleven slots name a maps\*.map.

level_table.description: Sixteen descriptor offsets; the descriptor's first word is its body offset and the map path follows it.

view_distance.description: How far a block may be and still be marked visible, in world units. 400, 700 or 2000 depending on the section; 1000:228B raises it to at least 1280 for the marking box.

fog_base.description: Where the depth ramp at DS:0x0FAE starts. With the view distance it determines the whole 2,048-byte ramp; 1000:0AE5 builds it.

depth_ramp.description: 2,048 bytes of fog band per unit of view depth, 0..63. Built by 1000:0AE5, or by 1000:0FB7 in the section that sets a view distance of 2000.

row_offsets.description: 200 words of 64000 - 320 * row: the framebuffer offset of a screen row, counting up from the bottom. This is why the projected y axis points up.

camera.description: The camera block: world x and world y as 24.8 fixed point, then XRot, YRot, a dead word and YShift. 1000:11C3 snapshots all six to DS:0x5D4C.

camera_snapshot.description: The frame's copy of the camera block. This, not DS:0x5D38, is what the transform reads.

camera_integer.description: The three words 1000:2433 subtracts from every vertex: world y, eye height, world x -- in that order, which is the order the view matrix's rows act in.

near_plane.description: The near clip depth. A shipped constant, 1; no instruction writes it.

eye_offset.description: Added to every view depth before the perspective divide. A shipped constant, 19.

reference_depth.description: The depth the frustum's half-extents are measured at. A shipped constant, 2048.

far_plane.description: The far clip depth. Ships 2040 but 1000:0AEA installs 1900 before anything draws.

viewport_selector.description: Chooses the 224x130 view or the 304x184 one, and the two lbm\gameover.bit origins with it. Ships zero and no instruction writes it, so only the narrow arm is reachable.

view_width.description: The view's width in pixels; 224 in the shipped build.

view_height.description: The view's height in pixels; 130 in the shipped build.

frustum_left.description: 2,048 words of the left x limit, indexed by view depth minus the near plane. 1000:3E68 builds this and the three that follow it.

frustum_right.description: 2,048 words of the right x limit.

frustum_lower.description: 2,048 words of the lower y limit.

frustum_upper.description: 2,048 words of the upper y limit.

sine_table.description: 1,280 words of round(0x7FFF * sin(2*pi*i/1024)). The cosine is the same table read 256 entries along, which is why it runs a quarter turn past the circle.

view_matrix.description: The frame's 4x4 view matrix, 1.15 fixed point, eight-byte row stride. Only the upper 3x3 is used.

visible_rooms.description: How many rooms the frame will walk; the far pointers are at DS:0x7700, up to sixteen.

room_list.description: Sixteen far pointers to rooms, 0xFFFFFFFF where unused.

visible_blocks.description: How many blocks 1000:2305 marked this frame.

draw_list_count.description: How many polygons survived the culls and reached the sorted draw list at DS:0x7826.

drawn_polygons.description: How many polygons 1000:3310 actually handed to a span routine.

blockset_slots.description: Blockset id to EMS slot, 0xFF where the blockset is not resident. Eighty slots, four to an EMS logical page.

blockset_shade_rows.description: Blockset id to a 256-byte row of the shade table at DS:0xBEBA. Shipped data; 0xFF means no ramp.

blockset_see_through.description: Blockset id to a see-through flag. Shipped data with eleven entries set; those blocksets get the masked column drawer and let a closed door show the room beyond.

detail_toggles.description: Six debug toggles a key handler cycles: DS:0x59A2 shading (0..2), DS:0x59A3 texturing (0/1), DS:0x59A4 detail level (0..2). They ship 1,1,2,1,2,1.

dark_mode.description: When set, a block's own light level at +0x12 is used instead of the flat 100. Ships zero.

arena_table.description: Sixteen (size, destination) pairs, terminated by 0xFFFF. 1000:7160 allocates them out of one block in table order, so they are contiguous.

map_header_segment.description: The map file's load segment. The solidity bitmap, the heights and the geometry follow it contiguously at +32, +2080 and +6176 paragraphs.

solid_map_segment.description: The 32,768-byte one-bit-per-cell solidity map, 32 world units to the cell.

height_map_segment.description: The 65,536-byte floor height map, 64 world units to the cell; bit 7 marks rough ground.

geometry_segment.description: The geometry section: rooms, block lists, blocks and vertices. Every pointer inside it is a byte offset from the map's first byte.

shade_table_segment.description: The 57,344-byte shade table, which is DARK.PAL or DAY.PAL loaded whole. 224 rows of 256.

framebuffer_segment.description: The 65,536-byte buffer the span routines draw into before it is blitted to 0xA000.

ems_page_frame.description: The EMS page-frame segment. Blockset slot s is at logical page (s >> 2) + 4, offset (s & 3) * 4096.

room_map_segment.description: The 128 x 128 coarse solidity map, built from the fine one by 1000:B2C5 rather than loaded.
